nucleotide analog reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs) may not be as effective as previously believed in preventing mucosal HIV infection.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the efficacy of nucleotide-based HIV prevention strategies may be limited by the natural dATPs present at the site of virus entry, and this limitation may be overcome by increasing the dNTP pool with nucleoside-based reverse transcriptase inhibitors.
